newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia coffee ouput could fall to 9.7 mln bags.
newsitem.headline: Colombia coffee ouput could fall to 9.7 mln bags.

text.p: Colombia's coffee output for the 1996/97 year seems set to come in at no higher than 9.7 million 60-kg bags, based on calculations from the National Coffee Federation's own estimates.
This week the federation reported a May harvest of 836,000 bags, taking the total for the first two months of the April/June quarter to 1.66 million bags.
The federation's estimate for the current quarter is for 3 million bags, or 1 million bags per month.

The October/December quarter came in at 3.6 million 60-kg bags, just below the initial forecast of 3.7 million bags, while output in the January/March quarter was 1.94 million bags against the 2.2 million bag estimate.
Even if the June forecast meets the 1 million bag target along with the 1.5 million bags estimated for July to September the total crop would still only be 9.7 million bags.
The lowest official estimate the federation has given for the 1996/97 coffee year so far is "about 10 million bags".
In a recent report, analysts Merill Lynch also indicated Colombia's 1996/97 coffee crop would fall below federation estimates, saying: "At best case scenario production might be 9.7 million bags."
